properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: NEWLY ADDED 2026-09-16 -- user-flagged that this feature, though already referenced in this dataset's own text (an earlier Block 3 note calls it 'a separate, physically distant open space between Blocks 15 and 7'), was never actually digitized as its own tracked polygon. Figure 6.2.3 labels 'LOUISIANA PASEO' directly as a landscaped pedestrian path running the full north-south length between Block 15 (west) and Blocks 7/11 (east), from Humboldt Street down to 23rd Street, opening into Power Station Park where Block 7 ends. Built here as a 6-vertex polygon using this project's own already-committed, GDAL/TPS-corrected corners for Block 15's east edge and Block 7/Block 11's west edges directly (not independently re-measured), so it shares an exact boundary with all three blocks by construction -- zero gap, zero overlap -- and its south end sits flush with Power Station Park's own west edge (also built from Block 11's same NW corner), so the two connect exactly as the diagram shows. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source URL cited for this file (the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the D4D, dead with a 404) is replaced by the final D4D (February 26, 2020), where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247) labels 'LOUISIANA PASEO' between Block 15 and Blocks 7/11, with Humboldt Street above, 23rd Street below and Power Station Park beside Blocks 7 and 11. Correction to the text above: the figure's label does not say 'landscaped'; D4D Section 4.25 describes the paseo as providing 'flexible-use urban plaza spaces and car-free pedestrian areas', and its enlargement concept plan is Figure 4.30.1. The committed geometry was not changed.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a simplified straight-sided approximation of a car-free pedestrian paseo; the final D4D's enlargement concept plan (Figure 4.30.1) shows it as a non-rectangular space with planting and plaza areas not captured here. Positional accuracy matches whatever the adjoining Block 15/7/11 files currently carry (see their own accuracy_caveat) since this polygon is built directly from their vertices.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows this polygon overlapping the active, unaddressed lots 4232011, 4232012 and 4175024 (all recorded 2022-08-30); the 2018 Draft EIR says the Port and City sub-areas have no Assessor's Block numbers and puts the privately owned remainder on Blocks 4175 and 4232.
properties.regulatory_context: A car-free, flexible-use pedestrian paseo and plaza space (D4D Sections 4.25 and 4.30), labelled 'LOUISIANA PASEO' on the final D4D's Figure 6.2.3 and running from Humboldt Street to 23rd Street between Block 15 and Blocks 7/11, opening into Power Station Park.
properties.notes: Newly added 2026-09-16; previously mentioned only in passing in other blocks' notes, never tracked as its own feature. Status 'planned': design review approved (annual reports: 8/3/21; memo June 2022) and no construction reported as of the March 2025 annual report. Use 'park': the final D4D treats it as open space (Section 4.25).
